ServiceGacc.faq1q: What is GACC registration and does it apply to US/UK exporters?
ServiceGacc.faq1a: GACC Decree 248 requires all overseas food manufacturers – including those in the US, UK, Canada and Australia – to register with the General Administration of Customs of China before exporting. Without registration, customs rejects your shipment at the border.
ServiceGacc.faq2q: How long does GACC registration take?
ServiceGacc.faq2a: Typical timelines are 2-4 months for low-risk categories and up to 6 months for high-risk foods. The exact duration depends on documentation completeness. We manage the entire CIFER process and track progress for you.
ServiceGacc.faq3q: What documents do I need for GACC registration?
ServiceGacc.faq3a: Key documents include business registration, HACCP certification, facility information, product specifications, and ingredient lists. We review, translate and submit all documentation through the CIFER system.
ServiceGacc.faq4a: No. Registration is valid for 5 years and renewal must be filed 6 months before expiry. We track your validity dates and handle renewals proactively.
ServiceGacc.faq5q: Who registers: the manufacturer or the exporter?
ServiceGacc.faq5a: The overseas manufacturing facility must be registered. If you manufacture in the US, UK, Australia or Canada and export to China, your production plant must be in the GACC registry – not just your trading company.
ServiceGacc.faq6q: Can I ship before registration is complete?
ServiceGacc.faq6a: No. Since January 1, 2022, Chinese customs rejects any food import without a valid GACC registration. Registration must be finalized before your first shipment.

ServiceLabel.faq1q: What does Chinese label compliance mean?
ServiceLabel.faq1a: Chinese labels must comply with GB 7718 (prepackaged food) and GB 28050 (nutrition labeling) standards. Unlike US or EU flexibility, all 9 mandatory elements must appear in Chinese or customs rejects the shipment.
ServiceLabel.faq2q: Can I use my existing label with a Chinese sticker?
ServiceLabel.faq2a: Yes, a Chinese sticker over your existing label is common practice. It must cover all mandatory elements and not contradict the original label. We verify consistency for you.
ServiceLabel.faq3q: What happens if my labels are non-compliant?
ServiceLabel.faq3a: Customs may reject your shipment, causing delays, storage fees and spoilage for perishable goods. Repeated violations can lead to fines and loss of import approval. Pre-shipment review is essential.
ServiceLabel.faq4q: Do you design the labels too?
ServiceLabel.faq4a: Yes. We create Chinese label layouts that meet all legal requirements and are print-ready, including production templates for your printer.
ServiceLabel.faq5q: Do I need separate labels for each product SKU?
ServiceLabel.faq5a: Generally yes, because each SKU has its own nutrition facts and ingredients. We provide efficient templates to cover multiple SKUs with minimal effort.
ServiceLabel.faq6q: What standards do labels need to comply with?
ServiceLabel.faq6a: The key standards are GB 7718-2025 (prepackaged food), GB 28050-2025 (nutrition labeling), plus product-specific standards such as GB 10344 for alcoholic beverages and GB 10765 for infant formula.

ServiceCosmetics.questionsSubtitle: Answers to the questions beauty brands ask most about NMPA filing, registration and cross-border sales in China.
ServiceCosmetics.faq1a: The NMPA (National Medical Products Administration) requires filing for ordinary imported cosmetics and registration for special-use products (sunscreen, whitening, hair dye). Without approval, selling in China is illegal – including via e-commerce platforms.
ServiceCosmetics.faq2q: What is the difference between filing and registration?
ServiceCosmetics.faq2a: Ordinary cosmetics (skincare, makeup, haircare) need only filing (notification). Special-use products (sunscreen, whitening, hair coloring) require full registration with stricter review, longer timelines and more documentation.
ServiceCosmetics.faq3q: Do I need a Chinese responsible person?
ServiceCosmetics.faq3a: Yes. Overseas manufacturers must designate a Chinese responsible agent who takes responsibility for product safety in China. We provide this agent for US, UK and global brands.
ServiceCosmetics.faq4q: Can I sell cosmetics via cross-border e-commerce without NMPA?
ServiceCosmetics.faq4a: Yes. Cross-border e-commerce channels (e.g., Tmall Global) allow sales without NMPA approval, as long as products stay in the cross-border channel. This is ideal for testing new products in the Chinese market.
ServiceCosmetics.faq5q: Does animal testing apply to imported cosmetics?
ServiceCosmetics.faq5a: Since 2021, animal testing is no longer mandatory for most imported cosmetics if safety assessment data is provided. Certain special-use products may still require testing.
ServiceCosmetics.faq6q: Can I update my formulation after NMPA filing?
ServiceCosmetics.faq6a: Substantive formulation changes require re-filing or re-registration. We advise which changes are permissible and which need a new submission.

ServiceBrand.faq1q: Why do I need trademark registration in China?
ServiceBrand.faq1a: China follows first-to-file: whoever registers the mark first with CNIPA owns it – even if that is a trademark squatter. Without your own registration, you risk market exclusion and costly litigation to get your brand back.
ServiceBrand.faq2q: How long does trademark registration take?
ServiceBrand.faq2a: CNIPA registration typically takes 9-12 months. Expedited examination is available when needed. We track progress and handle office actions for you.
ServiceBrand.faq3a: The Madrid System lets you extend a US or EU trademark to China with one international application via USPTO or EUIPO. However, direct CNIPA national filings are often more robust against attacks – we recommend the best strategy.
ServiceBrand.faq4q: How do I protect my brand on Alibaba and other online platforms?
ServiceBrand.faq4a: With a registered Chinese trademark, you can report and remove counterfeits on Alibaba, Tmall and JD. Customs IP recordal additionally lets Chinese customs seize fakes at the border.
ServiceBrand.faq5q: Can I use my existing US/EU trademark in China?
ServiceBrand.faq5a: No. A US or EU trademark offers no protection in China – only national registrations count. Your existing mark gives you no automatic rights in China; separate registration is mandatory.
ServiceBrand.faq6q: How do I monitor for trademark infringement in China?
ServiceBrand.faq6a: We monitor the CNIPA register and online platforms for similar marks and counterfeits. When violations appear, we file oppositions or enforcement actions – both preventive and reactive.

Faq.heroTitle: China Import Compliance: Frequently Asked Questions
Faq.heroSubtitle: Straight answers for exporters in the US, UK, Australia and New Zealand — covering GACC registration, CCC certification, Chinese labels, NMPA cosmetics filing and cross-border e-commerce.
Faq.gaccA1: GACC Decree 248 is China's regulation on the registration of overseas food manufacturers, processors, and storage facilities. It has been mandatory since January 1, 2022. All food exporters to China must be registered through China's CIFER system.
Faq.gaccQ2: How long does GACC registration take for my products?
Faq.gaccA2: It depends on your product category. Low-risk products can be registered directly through CIFER. High-risk products — such as dairy, meat and seafood — need a recommendation from your country's competent authority (for example USDA in the US or FSA in the UK). We manage the whole process for you.
Faq.gaccQ3: Is GACC registration really mandatory for every food product?
Faq.gaccA3: Yes — every food product exported to China needs GACC registration, whatever the product type or shipment volume. Without it, your goods simply will not clear Chinese customs.
Faq.gaccQ4: How long is a GACC registration valid?
Faq.gaccA4: GACC registration is valid for 5 years. Renewal applications must be submitted 3-6 months before expiration.
Faq.labelQ1: Do I really need Chinese labels to sell in China?
Faq.labelA1: Yes — Chinese labeling is mandatory for most imported products sold in China. Non-compliant labels can lead to customs rejection, product recalls and penalties, so it pays to get them right before you ship.
Faq.labelQ2: What must appear on a Chinese label?
Faq.labelA2: For prepackaged food, GB 7718-2025 requires: product name, ingredient list, net content, production/expiry date, storage conditions, manufacturer information, and Chinese agent details.
Faq.cccA1: CCC certification is mandatory for products in 17 categories including household appliances, IT equipment, lighting, automotive parts, children's toys, and lithium-ion batteries (added in 2024).
Faq.cccQ2: How long does CCC certification take?
Faq.cccA2: The process involves product testing, factory inspection and certification review, and the timeline depends on your product category. We coordinate every step with accredited Chinese testing labs.
Faq.cosmeticsQ1: What's the difference between ordinary and special cosmetics in China?
Faq.cosmeticsA1: Ordinary cosmetics — skincare, makeup and haircare — only need NMPA filing, which is relatively fast. Special cosmetics — sunscreen, whitening, hair dye and freckle-removal products — need full registration, which takes longer and involves more testing.
Faq.ecommerceQ1: Do I still need GACC registration for cross-border e-commerce?
Faq.ecommerceA1: Yes. Food sold through cross-border e-commerce still requires GACC registration. Some other requirements, like Chinese labels, may be relaxed for cross-border sales — but registration is not one of them.
Faq.ecommerceQ2: What are the purchase limits for cross-border e-commerce?
Faq.ecommerceA2: China's CBEC rules cap per-transaction and annual purchases per consumer. Within those limits, preferential tariff and tax rates apply — one of the main attractions of the cross-border channel.
Faq.brandQ1: Should I register my trademark before entering China?
Faq.brandA1: Absolutely. China runs a first-to-file trademark system — if you don't register, someone else can register your brand and block your market entry.
Faq.brandQ2: How long does trademark registration take?
Faq.brandA2: The process covers formal examination, a publication period and certificate issuance. Direct filing in China is generally faster than going through the Madrid System, and we recommend starting before your product launch.

Faq.gaccA5: Yes, a single overseas manufacturer can register products across multiple food categories under one GACC registration. Each category may have different documentation requirements, and we manage the full scope on your behalf.

DefinitionSchema.gaccName: GACC (General Administration of Customs of China)
DefinitionSchema.gaccDefinition: The General Administration of Customs of China (GACC) is the national customs authority responsible for regulating the import and export of goods, including food, cosmetics, and other consumer products entering the Chinese market.
DefinitionSchema.nmpaDefinition: The National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) is China's regulatory body overseeing cosmetics, medical devices, and pharmaceutical products. All imported cosmetics must be filed or registered with NMPA before sale in China.
DefinitionSchema.cccDefinition: China Compulsory Certification (CCC) is a mandatory product certification system for goods sold in the Chinese market. It ensures products meet Chinese safety, quality, and environmental standards.
DefinitionSchema.gb7718Definition: GB 7718-2025 is China's national standard for prepackaged food labeling. It specifies mandatory requirements for product names, ingredient lists, nutrition information, and other label elements.
DefinitionSchema.cbecDefinition: Cross-Border E-Commerce (CBEC) is a trade model that allows overseas businesses to sell directly to Chinese consumers through designated online platforms, with simplified customs procedures and tax treatment.
DefinitionSchema.ciferDefinition: CIFER is the China Import Food Enterprise Registration system. All overseas food manufacturers must register with GACC through the CIFER system before exporting food products to China.
DefinitionSchema.csarDefinition: CSAR is China's Cosmetic Supervision and Administration Regulation. It governs the registration, filing, production, and import of cosmetics in China, requiring product safety assessment and ingredient disclosure.
DefinitionSchema.decree248Definition: Decree 248 is GACC's regulation requiring registration of all overseas food production enterprises. Effective January 1, 2022, it expanded the scope from specific food categories to all food products imported into China.
DefinitionSchema.decree243Definition: Decree 243 is GACC's administrative measure for the safety of imported and exported food. It sets requirements for food safety management, labeling, and traceability for food importers and exporters in China.
DefinitionSchema.samrDefinition: SAMR is China's State Administration for Market Regulation. It oversees product quality, food safety standards, anti-monopoly enforcement, and market supervision. SAMR works with GACC on food and cosmetics regulation.

IndustryDairy.faq1q: Does my dairy product need GACC registration?

IndustryDairy.faq5q: Can chilled dairy products be imported?

IndustryMeat.faq2q: Which countries can export meat to China?
IndustryMeat.faq2a: Only countries with a bilateral market access agreement with China can export meat. The US, UK, Canada and Australia all have access for certain species - US beef and pork, UK lamb - with restrictions that change over time. We verify the current status for you.
IndustryMeat.faq3q: How long does meat product registration take?

IndustryMeat.faq4a: Imported meat needs Chinese labels with all mandatory elements under GB 7718, plus product-specific details such as origin, slaughter date and facility code. US and UK packaging must be reformatted for Chinese buyers.
IndustryMeat.faq5q: Do seafood and fish need the same registration as meat?
IndustryMeat.faq5a: Yes, seafood falls under CIFER registration too. Depending on category (farmed vs. wild-caught), additional traceability and health certificate requirements may apply - US and UK seafood exporters should prepare veterinary certificates early.
IndustryMeat.faq6q: Can we use the same registration for multiple product lines?

IndustryWine.faq3q: Should I register my wine brand trademark in China?
IndustryWine.faq3a: Absolutely. Wine and spirits brand names are frequently pre-registered by squatters in China. Unlike UKIPO or USPTO registration, protection in China comes only from a CNIPA trademark - early registration protects your label and prevents piracy.
IndustryWine.faq4q: How long does wine import registration take?
IndustryWine.faq4a: GACC registration typically takes 2-4 months. Label review and trademark registration (9-12 months) add to the timeline. We plan your full market entry, whether you export wine, whisky or other spirits.
IndustryWine.faq5q: Are there free trade agreements that reduce wine import duties?
IndustryWine.faq5a: Yes. Australia, Chile, New Zealand and Georgia enjoy tariff advantages for wine into China. US and UK wine and spirits face standard WTO duties - we calculate your effective tax burden for pricing.

IndustrySkincare.faq6q: Is trademark registration necessary for cosmetics brands?

BlogFaqGaccRegistrationGuide.faqQ1: What is GACC registration and who needs it?
BlogFaqGaccRegistrationGuide.faqA1: GACC registration is mandatory for every overseas food manufacturing, processing, and storage facility that exports to China. Introduced under Decrees 248 and 249 (January 1, 2022), it applies to all food products, and unregistered facilities cannot ship to China.
BlogFaqGaccRegistrationGuide.faqQ2: How long does GACC registration take?
BlogFaqGaccRegistrationGuide.faqA2: For the 18 high-risk food categories, registration goes through your country's competent authority and takes 2-6 months. For non-18-category products, direct CIFER system registration typically takes 2-4 weeks.
BlogFaqGaccRegistrationGuide.faqQ3: How long is a GACC registration valid?
BlogFaqGaccRegistrationGuide.faqA3: GACC registrations are valid for 5 years. Submit your renewal well before expiration, because once the deadline passes your products cannot enter China until the registration is renewed.
BlogFaqGaccRegistrationGuide.faqA4: You will need a business registration certificate, food production license, facility information (address, capacity, layout), a product list with HS/CIQ codes, quality management certificates (ISO 22000, HACCP, FSSC 22000), and current product labels for each SKU.
BlogFaqGaccRegistrationGuide.faqQ5: What happens if I don't register?
BlogFaqGaccRegistrationGuide.faqA5: Since January 1, 2022, Chinese customs has rejected shipments from unregistered facilities without exception; products are held at the port and either returned or destroyed.

BlogFaqChinaLabelCompliance.faqA1: Chinese label compliance means your product labels meet China's GB 7718 standard and any other applicable regulations. It is mandatory for all imported food and consumer products, and non-compliant labels result in customs rejection.
BlogFaqChinaLabelCompliance.faqQ2: What must be on a Chinese food label?
BlogFaqChinaLabelCompliance.faqA2: Product name, ingredient list, net content, manufacturer name and address, production date, shelf life, storage conditions, GACC registration number, country of origin, and Chinese distributor information, all in Simplified Chinese.
BlogFaqChinaLabelCompliance.faqA3: Yes, sticker labels are accepted as long as they meet GB 7718 requirements and are securely attached. That said, some distributors prefer direct printing for a more professional appearance.
BlogFaqChinaLabelCompliance.faqQ4: How long does label review take?
BlogFaqChinaLabelCompliance.faqA4: Professional label review typically takes 3-5 business days and covers checking every required element, verifying translations, and confirming compliance with the latest GB standards.

BlogFaqCccCertificationExplained.faqA1: CCC (China Compulsory Certification) is mandatory for products in 17 categories, whether imported into or manufactured in China, covering electronics, automotive parts, safety glass, children's toys, and more.
BlogFaqCccCertificationExplained.faqA2: Products in 17 categories: wires and cables, circuit switches, low-voltage electrical apparatus, small power motors, electric tools, welding machines, household appliances, audio/video equipment, IT equipment, lighting equipment, motor vehicles, safety glass, agricultural machinery, latex products, medical devices, fire fighting equipment, and security products.
BlogFaqCccCertificationExplained.faqQ3: How long does CCC certification take?
BlogFaqCccCertificationExplained.faqA3: Typically 3-6 months, depending on the product category and complexity. The process involves factory inspection, product testing at a designated Chinese laboratory, and documentation review.
BlogFaqCccCertificationExplained.faqA4: Typical costs range from $3,000 to $15,000+, including testing, factory inspection, and annual maintenance fees.

BlogFaqCosmeticsNmpaFiling.faqA1: NMPA (National Medical Products Administration) filing is mandatory for all cosmetics imported into China. Both ordinary and special-use cosmetics must be filed or registered before they can be sold.
BlogFaqCosmeticsNmpaFiling.faqQ2: What is the difference between ordinary and special-use cosmetics?
BlogFaqCosmeticsNmpaFiling.faqA2: Ordinary cosmetics include skincare, makeup, hair care, and perfume. Special-use cosmetics include sunscreens, hair dyes, hair growth products, hair removal products, and whitening or anti-freckle products.
BlogFaqCosmeticsNmpaFiling.faqQ3: How long does NMPA filing take?
BlogFaqCosmeticsNmpaFiling.faqA3: Ordinary cosmetics filing takes 4-6 months, while special-use cosmetics registration takes 8-12 months due to additional safety assessments and testing.
BlogFaqCosmeticsNmpaFiling.faqQ4: Do I need a Chinese responsible person?
BlogFaqCosmeticsNmpaFiling.faqA4: Yes. Overseas cosmetics companies must appoint a Chinese responsible person who handles NMPA filing, serves as the legal contact point in China, and assumes joint liability for product safety.

BlogFaqCrossBorderEcommerceChina.faqQ1: What is cross-border e-commerce (CBEC) in China?
BlogFaqCrossBorderEcommerceChina.faqA1: CBEC lets overseas brands sell directly to Chinese consumers through online platforms, bypassing traditional import channels. Products benefit from simplified regulatory requirements and lower tax rates.
BlogFaqCrossBorderEcommerceChina.faqQ2: What products can be sold through CBEC?
BlogFaqCrossBorderEcommerceChina.faqA2: China's Positive List covers more than 1,400 product categories, including most food products, cosmetics, health supplements, maternal and baby products, electronics, and more.
BlogFaqCrossBorderEcommerceChina.faqQ3: What are the advantages of CBEC compared with general trade?
BlogFaqCrossBorderEcommerceChina.faqA3: No CCC is required for many products, cosmetics benefit from simplified NMPA filing, certain food categories skip GACC registration, tax rates are lower (9.1% comprehensive tax versus 13% VAT plus consumption tax), and market entry is faster.
BlogFaqCrossBorderEcommerceChina.faqA4: Major platforms include Tmall Global, JD Worldwide, Kaola, Pinduoduo Global, and Douyin (TikTok) Global. Brands can also run their own cross-border e-commerce store.

BlogFaqKoreanCosmeticsGuide.faqQ1: Does a Korean cosmetics brand need NMPA filing for general trade imports?
BlogFaqKoreanCosmeticsGuide.faqA1: Yes. When you import cosmetics through general trade rather than cross-border e-commerce, every product must be either filed (ordinary cosmetics) or registered (special cosmetics) with the NMPA before import, regardless of the brand's country of origin.
BlogFaqKoreanCosmeticsGuide.faqQ2: Can I sell Korean cosmetics through cross-border e-commerce without NMPA filing?
BlogFaqKoreanCosmeticsGuide.faqA2: Yes, as an alternative. CBEC platforms such as Tmall Global and JD Worldwide allow cosmetics to be sold without NMPA filing as long as the products are on the Positive List. However, CBEC goods cannot be sold through offline retail or domestic e-commerce platforms. Many Korean brands use CBEC as a market-testing channel while preparing for full NMPA compliance.
BlogFaqKoreanCosmeticsGuide.faqQ3: Is a shampoo considered an ordinary or special cosmetic?
BlogFaqKoreanCosmeticsGuide.faqA3: A standard shampoo whose primary function is cleansing is an ordinary cosmetic, even if it carries scalp care or hair nourishment claims. However, a shampoo that explicitly claims anti-hair loss (防脱发) or hair growth promotion (育发/生发) crosses into special cosmetics territory and requires full registration.
BlogFaqKoreanCosmeticsGuide.faqQ4: How are scalp care and scalp essence products classified?
BlogFaqKoreanCosmeticsGuide.faqA4: It depends on the claims. A scalp product is an ordinary cosmetic when claims stay limited to moisturizing, nourishing, soothing, oil control, or dandruff control, and becomes a special cosmetic when claims include hair growth, anti-hair loss, or hair regrowth. The exact same formulation can be filed differently depending on the claims you make.
BlogFaqKoreanCosmeticsGuide.faqQ5: What happens if my cosmetics product is marketed for children or pregnant women?
BlogFaqKoreanCosmeticsGuide.faqA5: Stricter requirements apply. Products for children aged 12 and under require mandatory microbiological and toxicological testing with no animal testing exemption, a dedicated children's cosmetics evaluation, the 小金盾 (golden shield) icon on packaging, and a formulation limited to NMPA-approved children's ingredients. Products marketed as pregnancy-safe require adequate supporting safety data.
BlogFaqKoreanCosmeticsGuide.faqQ6: Can I use the same product formula I sell in Korea for the Chinese market?
BlogFaqKoreanCosmeticsGuide.faqA6: Not necessarily. Some ingredients approved by Korea's MFDS may be prohibited in China or subject to different concentration limits, so a full ingredient review against NMPA's prohibited and restricted lists is essential. NMPA also generally requires final filing or registration testing at CNAS-accredited Chinese laboratories.
BlogFaqKoreanCosmeticsGuide.faqQ7: How long does the NMPA cosmetics filing or registration process take?
BlogFaqKoreanCosmeticsGuide.faqA7: Timelines vary significantly. For ordinary cosmetics, the filing timeline depends on formula complexity, safety assessment readiness, and whether animal testing is required. Special cosmetics registration takes substantially longer because clinical efficacy testing at NMPA-accredited labs alone can take several months. The fastest path is ordinary cosmetics filing with a complete safety assessment and no children's claims.
BlogFaqKoreanCosmeticsGuide.faqQ8: What documents are required for NMPA cosmetics filing?
BlogFaqKoreanCosmeticsGuide.faqA8: Key documents for ordinary cosmetics filing include a complete product formula with concentrations, a Free Sale Certificate from MFDS with a notarized Chinese translation, a manufacturing license or GMP certificate, a product quality standard, label and packaging mockups, a safety assessment report, and a power of attorney appointing a Chinese responsible person. Special cosmetics require additional clinical efficacy test reports.
BlogFaqKoreanCosmeticsGuide.faqQ9: Can I file one product but sell multiple variants (different sizes, fragrances)?
BlogFaqKoreanCosmeticsGuide.faqA9: Generally, each variant needs its own filing. Products that differ in formulation, fragrance, color, or active ingredient concentration are treated as separate SKUs. Products that vary only in packaging size, with the same formula and different volumes, may share a filing under certain conditions.
BlogFaqKoreanCosmeticsGuide.faqQ10: Do I need a Chinese company to file cosmetics with NMPA?
BlogFaqKoreanCosmeticsGuide.faqA10: Yes. Every cosmetics product imported into China must have a Chinese domestic responsible person: a legal entity registered in China with a cosmetics-related business scope. This can be your own Chinese subsidiary, a distributor, or a third-party service provider. The responsible person is legally accountable for product safety and handles all NMPA communications.

AiAssistance.aboutContent: SinoTrade Compliance is a Shanghai-based regulatory compliance firm specializing in China market entry. Founded with 15+ years of expertise, we help exporters in 50+ countries navigate GACC registration, CCC certification, NMPA cosmetics filing, Chinese label compliance, cross-border e-commerce, and brand protection.
AiAssistance.faqQ1: What regulations apply to food products exported to China?
AiAssistance.faqA1: Food products exported to China must comply with GACC Decree 248 (registration of overseas food manufacturers), GACC Decree 249 (import and export food safety management), GB 7718 (labeling of prepackaged foods), and GB 28050 (nutrition labeling).
AiAssistance.faqQ2: Do all products need CCC certification?
AiAssistance.faqA2: No. CCC certification is mandatory only for products in 17 defined categories including electronics, household appliances, automotive parts, lighting, safety glass, and children toys. Products outside these categories may still need other certifications.
AiAssistance.faqQ3: How long does GACC registration take?
AiAssistance.faqA3: Standard GACC registration typically takes 6-10 weeks from submission of complete documentation. Registration for high-risk categories (18 categories) may take longer as it requires approval from the competent authority in the exporting country.
